David C. Graham

Libertarian candidate for United States Senator, Kansas · Challenger

Attorney (Overland Park, Kansas)

David C. Graham is an Overland Park attorney and the Libertarian Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Kansas in the November 3, 2026 general election. He is running against Republican incumbent Roger Marshall and Democrat Adam Hamilton. He has said he ran for U.S. Senate in 2022 as well.

Where Graham stands

Tariffs and trade
Calls a tariff a tax and says most tariffs today are ill-advised. Opposes tariffs on food and says the current administration's on-and-off tariff changes leave the market without predictability.
Iran war
Says he would vote to end U.S. involvement in the Iran war. Wants Congress to hold a vote on a declaration of war, and says he would vote no.
Health care / Medicaid
Supports moving to a free-market health care system and away from taxpayer-funded programs, including Medicare and Medicaid. Says Medicare should not end immediately and that people who rely on it should be provided for during the transition.
Abortion
Describes himself as a pro-life Libertarian and says a separate human being exists from the point of fertilization. He is endorsed by the Pro-Life Libertarian caucus.
Cost of living / regulation
Proposes abolishing the Departments of Education and Energy and cutting federal regulations and agencies. Says lower regulatory costs would reduce prices for goods and services.
Taxes and size of government
Supports less government and lower taxes.
Ukraine
Says he would vote to end U.S. involvement in the war in Ukraine, arguing the U.S. has no direct, immediate interest in it.
Marijuana
Supports legalizing marijuana.
Second Amendment
Describes himself as strong on the Second Amendment.

Background

  • Attorney in private practice, Overland Park, Kansas
  • J.D., University of Kansas School of Law
  • B.A., political science and philosophy, Washburn University
  • Graduate of Shawnee Mission North High School
  • Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senate, Kansas, 2022 (per Johnson County Post interview)
